newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian stocks stumble at end of strong year.
newsitem.headline: Canadian stocks stumble at end of strong year.

text.p: Toronto stocks ended their final session of the year on a weak note Tuesday, tugged down by weaker U.S. markets and profit-taking.
The TSE 300 Composite Index sank 27.22 points to 5,927.03 with 44.26 million shares worth C$574 million (US$418.8 million) trading hands.

Despite Tuesday's drop, the market made substantial gains for the year. The TSE 300 rose 25.7 percent, up 1,213.49 points from last year's close at 4,713.54. Trading value totalled C$301 billion (US$220 billion), almost C$100 billion (US$73 billion) more than in 1995.
"That's not bad. I'll take it. I hope we can duplicate it next year, which I'm assuming here in Canada we can do," Fred Ketchen, senior vice-president of ScotiaMcLeod Inc., said.
In the broader market, advancers led decliners 525 to 359 with 307 unchanged in Tuesday's action.
"We've lost about half of what we gained yesterday, led lower not by anything domestic but probably by the weakeness in the U.S. markets," Ketchen said.
The Dow Jones industrial average fell 101.10 points to 6,448.27, hurt by a weak bond market and last-minute profit-taking. The Dow gained 26 percent for the year after a rise of 33.5 percent in 1995.
"Other than that, I think there's some profit-taking after some increases in stock prices in Canada yesterday," Ketchen said.
The TSE 300 leaped 51.64 points on Monday, led by large, blue-chip stocks.
But several big blue-chips ended lower Tuesday, with Seagram Co. falling C$2.35 to close at C$54.25, Placer Dome Inc. off C$0.85 to end at C$30.05 and BCE Inc. dropping 0.85 to C$65.30.
Among other gauges, consumer products lost the most, dropping 2.13 percent, followed by conglomerates, which slid 1.59 percent.
